questions.question: Are the deleted listeners (device-sync.ts:874-892, task-store.tsx:181-255) actually removed from the source, not merely disabled behind a flag or commented out, with task-store.tsx consuming projected state via react-engine-hooks exclusively -- verified by absence of the dead code, not just a passing test that happens not to exercise it?

Are the deletions in device-sync.ts and task-store.tsx limited to removals only, with zero new branches or exported functions introduced (per scope.excludes / Boundary Rule 5), and is src/store/persistence.ts's legacy read/write path against notestr:events:${groupId} retired consistent with the module map's 'DEPRECATED -- removed Phase 8' status?

Could `task-store` be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its `dependencies_allowed` list (react-engine-hooks' exposed projected state)? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist and do they flow through declared seam contracts in architecture.md?

Does task-store.listener-removal.test.tsx assert the removed listeners no longer fire on a simulated applicationMessage event (behavioral proof, not just a grep for absent code), and do the pre-existing S8/S11-dependent test suites (react-engine-hooks, recovery) remain green after this removal, confirming the new paths fully cover what the deleted listeners provided per this story's dependency note?

Is this story sequenced after S8 (react-engine-hooks), S10 (publish-outbox), and S11 (recovery-sequencing) are all complete, so the deleted listeners' responsibilities (projection updates, publish/outbox, recovery) are fully covered by the new engine paths before removal -- verified by which stories' tests exist and pass at the time this story lands?

Does removing src/store/persistence.ts's legacy read/write path avoid leaving an orphaned IDB namespace with no migration/cleanup story -- documented as an accepted risk if data is simply abandoned in place, or actively cleaned up if not?

does the implementation satisfy AC-MIG-3's observable -- does a grep-based test assert zero matches for applicationMessage in src/store/task-store.tsx, run as the Phase-8 exit gate, with evidence that the pre-Phase-8 tree had exactly one such match (task-store.tsx:181-255) so the check is state-discriminating across the phase boundary rather than trivially true before this story ran too?

task-store.tsx's EngineTaskBridge now consumes deferred-store.ts's createPersistenceAdapter() (the real, durable ten-method S11 adapter) in place of S9's session-scoped interim in-memory one -- was this swap actually required by this story's scope, or is it an undeclared scope expansion? (Answer basis: origin-routing correctness -- the story's own explicit mandate -- is meaningless against an adapter whose loadCheckpoint never survives a reload; the swap is a load-bearing precondition for the origin-routing requirement, not an independent improvement. Verify no other file outside scope.includes needed to change to support this, and that deferred-store.ts's own test suite -- unchanged -- still passes.)

TaskStoreProvider's origin-routing effect falls back to origin:'welcome' if loadCheckpoint(groupId) rejects (IDB quota/eviction/private-mode). For a group that DOES have a real prior checkpoint, a transient read failure therefore routes to a fresh 'welcome' bootstrap instead of 'restored' recovery on that one attempt -- is this the correct degrade-not-crash choice (matching the pre-existing synchronous-gate precedent elsewhere in this file), and does it converge safely (no duplicate/lost tasks) given the engine's own idempotent accepted-log dedup, rather than needing a retry-the-loadCheckpoint-call design?

Is the new restored-origin/recovery durability path (TaskStoreProvider -> loadCheckpoint -> engine.start({origin:'restored'}) -> AC-REC-9 routing -> R1 projection rebuild) actually exercised by a real, non-mocked-persistence integration test post-S12 (not just unit-level receive-engine.recovery tests against a hand-built PersistenceAdapter), given this story is the FIRST production composition root to wire the real deferred-store.ts adapter in at all?

device-sync.ts's publishTaskStateSync (the new-member task-state snapshot sent on invite) now reads from the durable engine accepted-log instead of the legacy per-group event log -- for a group CREATOR (never routes through the engine's fetchBootstrap join-time path, since no kind-30078 snapshot targets them) whose own tasks arrive solely via ReceiveEngine.acceptLocal (S14) on their own dispatches, does the accepted-log reliably contain the creator's own task history by the time they invite a new member, with no dependency on the creator's browser having been reloaded/recovered first?
